metaDescription: Five dual-band smart plugs that connect to 5GHz Wi-Fi, compared on power rating, energy monitoring, outdoor use and setup, for homes with newer routers.
introParagraphs: Most smart plugs only speak 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, and that quietly causes more setup failures than any other detail. If your router merges its bands under one network name, or your phone insists on joining the faster 5GHz side, the plug may refuse to pair and offer no useful error. A plug that supports 5GHz, or at least handles both bands, removes that whole category of frustration.

The five plugs below all advertise dual-band support, and they range from slim indoor models to an outdoor two-outlet unit. We separated them by power rating, extra features like energy monitoring, and the way each one handles setup. Variant listings that differ only in pack size were treated as one product, so the picks represent distinct hardware.
These plugs were evaluated from product specs and buyer feedback, not paid placement. The goal is to help you choose a plug that connects to the network you already have.

products.name: EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A WiFi Outlet
products.description:
The EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A is the most balanced pick for a typical home with a modern router. It supports the 5GHz band alongside 2.4GHz, and the listing promises quicker response times than plugs stuck on the older band. The plug is rated for 120V and 15A, which equals 1800W, enough for lamps, fans and higher-draw kitchen items such as a coffee maker.

Setup uses Bluetooth to find the plug, then moves the connection onto your Wi-Fi, which reduces the guesswork of a manual pairing. Voice control works through Alexa and Google Home, so you can switch devices with a spoken command. It is sold in four-pack and two-pack formats, but the hardware is the same.

The tradeoff is that this model has no energy monitoring, so you will not see how much power a device draws. Compared with the EIGHTREE four-pack that adds monitoring, this one is the plainer choice, but it keeps the setup simpler. At 1800W it is rated higher in wattage terms than a basic lamp plug, though you should still keep heat-producing appliances away unless the rating clearly covers them. For most buyers, it is the plug to start with.
products.bestFor: A household that wants reliable 5GHz pairing and 1800W of capacity without extra features.
pros: Pairs on 5GHz as well as 2.4GHz networks
1800W rating covers lamps, fans and coffee makers
Bluetooth setup takes the guesswork out of pairing
Alexa and Google voice control both supported
cons: No energy monitoring in this version

products.name: GHome Smart 5G 15A WiFi Smart Plug
products.description:
The GHome Smart 5G plug stands out because its listing names its safety marks: ETL and FCC certified. Those marks matter when you are plugging a coffee maker or similar appliance into a device you did not choose from a household-name brand. It is rated at 120V and 15A, giving the same 1800W ceiling as the EIGHTREE 15A plug.

The plug combines Bluetooth setup with dual-band Wi-Fi, and the listing recommends using the 5GHz band for peak performance near the router. Alexa and Google Home voice control are supported, and a timer function schedules devices on and off. It is sold in several pack sizes, all of which count as one product here.

The tradeoff is a lack of energy monitoring, so it shares a limitation with the EIGHTREE 15A plug. The brand is less familiar than some, so the app and support depth are reasons to read the manual. Compared with the EIGHTREE four-pack that includes energy monitoring and a pass-through design, the GHome is a simpler plug. It is a strong match when certification is your tiebreaker.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want visible ETL and FCC marks on a 5GHz plug powering a kitchen appliance.

1800W rating suits coffee makers and fans
Suggests the 5GHz band near the router

cons: Less established brand than larger rivals

products.name: EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug Energy Monitoring 4 Pack
products.description:
This EIGHTREE four-pack is the one to choose when you want to see what your devices actually use. Its energy monitoring function gives usage patterns so you can spot power-hungry devices and decide what deserves a schedule. It supports both 5GHz and 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, so it pairs in the same way as the standard EIGHTREE plug.

The body is compact enough that two plugs can share a single wall outlet, a real help on a crowded duplex. The listing notes ETL and FCC listing, which puts it on par with the GHome 5G plug in terms of safety marks. Voice control and app control follow the same pattern as the others in this lineup.

The cost of the extra capability is that the monitoring data lives in the brand's app, and a monitoring plug is only useful if you will look at the numbers. For a household that just wants lamps on a timer, the EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A is simpler. Compared with the NOUS A9, which also tracks energy, the EIGHTREE gives you more plugs in the box and a pass-through friendly shape, while the NOUS leans on the Tuya app ecosystem.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants to learn which devices drive their power use while staying on 5GHz.

products.name: NOUS A9 Wi-Fi Smart Plug 15A Dual-Band
products.description:
The NOUS A9 makes its dual-band claim loudly, pointing out that unlike most smart plugs limited to older bands it also supports 5GHz Wi-Fi. It adds real-time energy monitoring, with consumption reports delivered in the app. Its 15A rating matches the rest of the lineup, and it works with Alexa, Google Home and the Tuya app.

Because it uses the Tuya app, it fits well into homes that already run other Tuya-based devices, since they all appear in one place. Voice control lets you manage appliances hands-free, and schedules cover daily routines. The energy reports help identify devices that draw more than you expect.

The tradeoff is that the brand is less common, so support and replacement options may be harder to find than for larger names. It lists fewer certification details than the GHome or the monitoring EIGHTREE four-pack, so check the housing marks on the unit you receive. Compared with the EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug, the NOUS stays indoors, and compared with the standard EIGHTREE 15A, it adds monitoring. Choose it if the Tuya app is already on your phone.

products.name: EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug with 2 Outlets
products.description:
The EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug is the only outdoor choice in this lineup, and it carries two outlets that work independently. That lets you run patio lights on one socket and a fountain on the other, each with its own schedule. It supports 5GHz and 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and switches between the bands automatically in dual-band unified mode.

The IP44 rating protects against splashes and light moisture, which suits a covered porch or a protected outdoor wall. It is a splash rating rather than a heavy-weather rating, so place it under cover and off the ground. Timer functions let you set the lights to come on in the evening and shut off at a set hour.

The tradeoff is that this unit is outdoors only in intent, and it is bulkier than the slim indoor plugs. The listing does not give an amperage, so check the rating before connecting heavy loads. Compared with the standard EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A, which is made for indoor appliances, this one trades slimness for weather protection. If your need is a backyard, this is the only pick here that fits.
products.bestFor: A covered patio or deck where lights and a fountain need separate schedules on a 5GHz network.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Many plugs advertise Wi-Fi without saying which band, and most older designs only work on 2.4GHz. Look for the words 5GHz or dual-band on the listing, not just the box art. The EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A, the GHome Smart 5G and the NOUS A9 all state band support clearly. A plug that handles both bands is safer if your router later changes its settings.

The rating tells you what the plug can carry. The EIGHTREE 15A, the GHome 5G and the energy-monitoring EIGHTREE four-pack sit at a 120V and 15A rating, or 1800W for the first two. Match this number to the appliance label, and leave headroom for startup surges. Heat-producing items such as space heaters deserve extra caution even when the rating appears sufficient.

Marks like ETL and FCC indicate third-party testing and radio compliance. The GHome Smart 5G lists both, and the EIGHTREE energy-monitoring four-pack lists them too. The NOUS A9 listing does not state them in the brief, so look at the product itself when it arrives. A plug powering a coffee maker or fan should carry visible certification, not just a marketing claim.

Monitoring turns a plug into a small meter, showing how much power a device uses over time. The EIGHTREE energy-monitoring four-pack and the NOUS A9 both include it, while the EIGHTREE 15A and GHome 5G do not. The data is only worth having if you will read it, so skip it if you want simple timers. If you do use it, check one device at a time to find standby waste.

A bulky plug can cover the second outlet on a wall plate and force you to use an extension cord. The EIGHTREE energy-monitoring four-pack is shaped so two plugs can fit into one outlet. Outdoor units like the EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug are inherently larger because of their weather protection. Measure the space behind a bed or sofa before choosing.

Indoor plugs do not belong on a porch, because moisture and dust shorten their life and create safety issues. The EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug has an IP44 rating for splashes and light moisture, and it still needs a covered spot. The other four picks are for indoor use only. Pick the plug for the room it will actually live in.

howWeEvaluated.title: Band support and connection reliability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked how clearly each plug states its Wi-Fi support. The NOUS A9, GHome 5G and both EIGHTREE indoor plugs name 5GHz, while the outdoor EIGHTREE adds a unified mode that moves between bands. This score reflects listed specs and buyer feedback on pairing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power rating and safety marks
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored plugs that state a 120V and 15A rating and show ETL or FCC listing. The GHome 5G and the energy-monitoring EIGHTREE four-pack lead on visible certification. The NOUS A9 lost points for listing fewer compliance details in the brief.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extra features
howWeEvaluated.description: Energy monitoring, two-in-one-outlet shapes and independent outlets all earned credit. The EIGHTREE four-pack and NOUS A9 lead on monitoring, and the outdoor EIGHTREE leads on outlet count. Plain plugs scored well when they kept setup simple.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup simplicity
howWeEvaluated.description: Bluetooth-assisted pairing helps people get on Wi-Fi without wrestling band settings. The EIGHTREE 15A and the GHome 5G both use it, which is why they sit near the top. Plugs that depend on a third-party app, like the NOUS A9 with Tuya, scored slightly lower for newcomers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A leads as the all-rounder, the GHome 5G on certification, the monitoring EIGHTREE and NOUS on data, and the outdoor EIGHTREE on weather protection. Each pick covers a distinct need rather than repeating the same hardware.

cards.label: 5GHz band
cards.text: The 5GHz band offers faster speeds and less crowding, but it covers a smaller area and passes through walls less well. The EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A and the GHome Smart 5G plug both claim the benefits of this band near the router. It is ideal for plugs in the same room or one wall away from the access point. Choose it when your router is close and your 2.4GHz channel is busy.

cards.label: 2.4GHz band
cards.text: The 2.4GHz band reaches farther and penetrates walls better, which helps outbuildings and distant bedrooms. The EIGHTREE Outdoor Smart Plug and NOUS A9 handle both bands, so they can fall back to 2.4GHz when 5GHz is weak. Pick a dual-band plug and let it choose the better signal. If your outlet is far from the router, the longer reach matters more than speed.

howToChoose.note: If you are unsure, buy a plug that supports both bands and let the router decide.

faq.q: Do I need a 5GHz smart plug?
faq.a: Not always. A 2.4GHz plug works fine if your router broadcasts that band, and many routers keep it on by default. A 5GHz-capable plug helps when you have turned 2.4GHz off or when your phone will not stay on the right band during setup. A dual-band plug like the EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A is the safe choice.

faq.q: Why does my smart plug fail to connect?
faq.a: The most common cause is a phone connected to 5GHz while the plug expects 2.4GHz. Moving your phone to the 2.4GHz band or splitting the router's bands usually fixes it. Plugs that support both bands, such as the NOUS A9 and the GHome Smart 5G, reduce this problem. Bluetooth-assisted setup also helps.

faq.q: Which 5GHz smart plug is best overall?
faq.a: The EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A is our overall pick because it supports 5GHz, carries an 1800W rating and keeps setup simple with Bluetooth. If you want energy data, step up to the EIGHTREE four-pack or the NOUS A9. For visible certification marks, consider the GHome Smart 5G.

faq.q: Can I plug a coffee maker into a smart plug?
faq.a: Yes, if the plug's rating covers the appliance. The EIGHTREE and GHome plugs are rated at 120V and 15A, which equals 1800W, and their listings mention coffee makers. The machine needs a physical switch left on, and some models need a button press after power returns. Check the label for wattage first.

It is worth it if you want to find devices that waste power or confirm a schedule is saving energy. The EIGHTREE energy-monitoring four-pack and the NOUS A9 both include it. If your goal is simply to turn a lamp on at dusk, a plain plug is easier and less expensive.

faq.q: Can I use these plugs outdoors?
faq.a: Only the EIGHTREE 5GHz Outdoor Smart Plug is designed for it. It has an IP44 rating, which resists splashes and light moisture, but it should still sit under cover and off the ground. The four indoor plugs have no weather protection and should stay inside.

faq.q: How many plugs should I buy in a pack?
faq.a: Count the devices you would actually schedule, such as two lamps, a fan and a coffee maker, then add one spare. The EIGHTREE and GHome plugs come in several pack sizes with identical hardware, so a larger pack only saves effort if you will use every plug. Unused plugs sitting in a drawer are the real waste. A single plug is a fine way to test whether 5GHz pairing works in your home.

faq.q: Will a smart plug make my appliance safer to leave on?
faq.a: Not by itself. A plug controls power, but it does not add protection to a heating element or detect a fault in the appliance. Listed overload protection and ETL marks add some assurance, and the GHome Smart 5G lists both ETL and FCC. For anything that gets hot, treat the plug as a convenience and stay with the appliance's own safety features.

faq.q: Do smart plugs keep working if the internet goes down?
faq.a: Schedules stored on the plug can sometimes continue, but remote and voice control generally depend on your Wi-Fi and the maker's cloud service. Plugs like these route through brand apps, so a service outage can interrupt control. Matter-certified plugs handle local control better, though none in this lineup lists Matter.
